reasoning: The fixed thresholds and marking rule give at most A+B+C deletion operations, so termination is finite. Charging each removed edge to its first deletion partitions the removed weight into disjoint charges. Each left-node operation removes less than M_0/(8A), and there are at most A such operations; thus left-node charges total at most M_0/8. The corresponding right-node and group bounds give total removed weight at most 3M_0/8, leaving at least 5M_0/8. At termination every undeleted node/group has weight at least its relevant threshold, since otherwise it remains eligible. Any label incident to a retained edge is necessarily undeleted: deleting that label removed all its then-remaining incident edges, and edges never return. This establishes the threshold claim even for labels incident to zero-weight edges; S4's positive-weight qualification does not limit its preceding general argument.
